body: According to the opinion, Stradtman Park, LLC borrowed $3.6 million from KeyBank National Association in July 2014 on a commercial property valued at about $7 million. In October 2014 KeyBank assigned the loan to Wilmington Trust, National Association, as trustee for JPMBB Commercial Mortgage Securities Trust 2014-C24, and it was placed in a CMBS under a pooling and servicing agreement the borrower did not sign. LNR Partners, LLC was to act as special servicer if the loan became distressed or defaulted.

The borrower paid as required from 2014 into early 2020: $18,779.30 a month in principal and interest and $20,300.39 a month in reserves, for $39,079.69 in all. In 2019 it asked for approvals and reserve payments for lease renewals, expansions and contractor repairs, and although the loan was performing, LNR handled those requests; the borrower says LNR was obstructive and forced it to pay costs itself. From May 2020 the borrower paid only principal and interest and directed that its payments be applied that way, but the lender side spread them across principal, interest and reserves, which produced a default. In November 2020 the borrower stopped remitting rents, and the trustee later sued to foreclose.

Erie County Supreme Court granted the trustee partial summary judgment on foreclosure and rents, which the borrower did not appeal, and then held a damages hearing. Justice Emilio Colaiacovo's amended order and judgment, entered May 21, 2025, awarded the full $583,938.25 in default-rate interest requested but refused $120,882.59 more in note-rate interest, because the default rate was five points above the note rate and the trustee had not documented its calculation. On fees, the borrower's expert put customary Western New York commercial foreclosure rates at $350 to $450 an hour, while the trustee's witness said LNR paid $650 to $800 for partners and $350 to $575 for associates, and the invoices did not show the rate for each charge. The court found the rates unreasonable and many charges "duplicative and exaggerated," awarded $250,000 of the roughly $588,000 sought, and said the trustee had come "perilously close" to having the entire judgment vacated over its fee request.

The Fourth Department affirmed. It acknowledged that unambiguous contracts are enforced as written but noted that a foreclosure invokes the court's equitable powers. It held that the plaintiff bears the burden of proving damages, that the duplicative-interest ruling was supported by a fair interpretation of the evidence, and that contractual fees are enforceable only to the extent reasonable and warranted for services actually rendered. It found no abuse of discretion in the $250,000 award and rejected the trustee's remaining challenges.

timeline.label: Stradtman Park, LLC takes a $3.6 million loan from KeyBank on a commercial property
Loan assigned to the JPMBB 2014-C24 CMBS trust; LNR Partners designated special servicer in the event of distress or default
Borrower begins paying principal and interest only, withholding reserve deposits
Borrower stops remitting rents; trustee later sues to foreclose
Erie County Supreme Court enters amended order and judgment awarding $250,000 of about $588,000 in requested fees and denying duplicative note-rate interest
Appellate Division, Fourth Department unanimously affirms
